body.en: Unit 2 treats exponential and logarithmic functions as models of multiplicative change — quantities that change by a constant factor over equal intervals, rather than a constant additive amount.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Exponential Functions, Multiplicative Rates & Natural Base e

body.en: Construct exponential functions \(f(x) = ab^x\), distinguish growth from decay, and model discrete geometric compounding.

Domain: \((-\infty, \infty)\). Range: \((0,\infty)\) when \(a>0\). Horizontal asymptote: \(y=0\).

Key property: Over equal intervals \(\Delta x\), outputs multiply by the same factor \(b^{\Delta x}\).

Growth: \(b>1\). Decay: \(0Natural base: \(e\approx2.71828\).

\[f(x)=ae^{kx}:\quad k>0\implies\text{growth},\quad k<0\implies\text{decay}.\]

An initial population of 500 bacteria triples every 6 hours. Write an exponential function \(P(t)\) for the population after \(t\) hours, and evaluate the population at \(t = 12\) hours.

The base is 3 and the time period for tripling is 6 hours: \[ P(t) = 500 \cdot 3^{t/6}. \]

At \(t = 12\): \[ P(12) = 500 \cdot 3^{12/6} = 500 \cdot 3^2 = 500 \cdot 9 = 4,500\text{ bacteria}. \]

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

An antique clock was purchased for $1,200 and increases in value by 5% each year. Write an exponential model \(V(t)\) for its value after \(t\) years, and determine its value after 3 years to the nearest dollar.

solution.en:
The growth factor is \(b = 1 + 0.05 = 1.05\). The model is: \[ V(t) = 1200(1.05)^t. \]

For \(t = 3\): \[ V(3) = 1200(1.05)^3 = 1200(1.157625) = 1,389.15. \] Rounded to the nearest dollar, the value is $1,389.

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Continuous Compounding, Half-Life & Doubling Models

body.en: Model continuous exponential processes using base \(e\), calculate decay half-lives, and evaluate continuous interest.

label.en: ▲ AP Exam Traps & Pitfalls — Exponential & Logarithmic Functions

body.en:
• Domain of Logarithms: In \(\log_b(g(x))\), the argument must be strictly positive: \(g(x) > 0\). Always test for extraneous solutions that produce non-positive arguments.
  • Base vs. Continuous Rate: The annual growth factor \(b\) in \(ab^t\) relates to the continuous rate \(r\) by \(b = e^r\). Do not confuse \(r = 0.05\) in \(e^{0.05t}\) with \((1.05)^t\); \(e^{0.05} \approx 1.0513\).
  • Logarithm Laws: \(\log(A+B) \neq \log A + \log B\)! Log of a product is sum of logs: \(\log(AB) = \log A + \log B\).
  • Semi-log Linearity: If a scatter plot of \((x, \ln y)\) is linear, then \(y\) is an exponential function of \(x\). If \((\ln x, \ln y)\) is linear, then \(y\) is a power function \(y = ax^k\).

A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 24 days. Starting with 80 grams, how much remains after 72 days?

Use the half-life model: \[ A(t) = A_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/h} = 80\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/24}. \]

Substitute \(t = 72\): \[ A(72) = 80\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{72/24} = 80\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = 80 \times \frac{1}{8} = 10\text{ grams}. \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

An investment of $5,000 grows at an annual rate of 6% compounded continuously according to \(A(t) = 5000e^{0.06t}\). In how many years will the investment double in value? Express your answer analytically in terms of natural logarithms and compute to the nearest tenth of a year.

solution.en:
Set the future value to twice the principal: \[ 5000e^{0.06t} = 10000 \implies e^{0.06t} = 2. \]

Take the natural logarithm: \[ 0.06t = \ln(2) \implies t = \frac{\ln(2)}{0.06}. \]

Evaluating numerically: \[ t \approx \frac{0.693147}{0.06} \approx 11.55\text{ years}. \] Rounded to the nearest tenth: 11.6 years.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Logarithmic Inverses, Semi-Log Plots & Analytical Equation Solving

body.en: Utilize logarithmic properties to invert exponential functions, linearize exponential data on semi-log scales, and solve transcendental equations.

Definition of Logarithm: \(y = \log_b x \iff b^y = x\) for \(b>0, b\neq 1, x>0\).

Core Properties:

\[ \log_b(xy) = \log_b x + \log_b y, \quad \log_b\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = \log_b x - \log_b y, \quad \log_b(x^k) = k\log_b x. \]

Semi-Log Model: If \(y = ab^x\), taking natural logs yields: \[ \ln y = \ln(a) + x\ln(b). \] Letting \(Y = \ln y\), \(m = \ln b\), and \(k = \ln a\), this produces the linear equation \(Y = mx + k\).

Solve the logarithmic equation \(\ln(x+2) + \ln(x-1) = \ln(10)\) analytically for all real solutions.

Step 1: Combine logs on the left: \[ \ln((x+2)(x-1)) = \ln(10) \implies (x+2)(x-1) = 10. \]

Step 2: Expand and set to zero: \[ x^2 + x - 2 = 10 \implies x^2 + x - 12 = 0 \implies (x+4)(x-3) = 0. \]

Potential solutions: \(x = -4\) and \(x = 3\).

Step 3: Check domain restrictions: For \(x = -4\), \(\ln(x-1) = \ln(-5)\) is undefined (extraneous). For \(x = 3\), both \(3+2=5>0\) and \(3-1=2>0\) are valid. Therefore, the only real solution is \(x = 3\).

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Data pairs \((x, y)\) are plotted on a semi-log grid where \(Y = \ln(y)\). The resulting linear regression line has the equation \(Y = 0.35x + 1.20\). Express \(y\) as an exponential function of \(x\) in the form \(y = ab^x\), rounding \(a\) and \(b\) to three decimal places.

solution.en:
Exponentiate both sides with base \(e\): \[ \ln(y) = 0.35x + 1.20 \implies y = e^{0.35x + 1.20} = e^{1.20} \cdot e^{0.35x} = e^{1.20} \cdot (e^{0.35})^x. \]

Compute the coefficients: \[ a = e^{1.20} \approx 3.3201 \approx 3.320, \] \[ b = e^{0.35} \approx 1.41907 \approx 1.419. \]

Thus the exponential function is \(y = 3.320(1.419)^x\).
